I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the system I know best, it fits the local water and temperature conditions, and at my age I would rather do the crops I can manage steadily than chase something unfamiliar. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will focus on feeding it, watering it at the key stages, and keeping disease and weeds under control. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away to use the full season and keep total output high from the same land.

I will not spread myself across too many crops. I would rather manage two staple crops well than manage several crops badly. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and a few timely irrigations because wheat here responds well to water at jointing and grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me more stable yield, and I will push nitrogen a bit more than wheat while watching pests around seedling and ear stages. I will use ploughing ahead of wheat and rotary tillage ahead of maize because that is practical for me and matches the rotation. My goal is stable grain yield, manageable fieldwork, and lower risk.
